solver: Not the solver: cmd/candbench is a microbenchmark of internal/cand alone. Input is a snapshot (empty, or a -sol mid-solve solution JSON) plus the round's hot cells; output is the candidate set per (demand, slot) family with timings, BFS counters and a brute-force recall comparison. No MIP, no objective, no search.
why: The outer-loop A/B cannot measure the candidate layer: one round costs a Gurobi solve whose run-to-run spread is ~7.7% on setA-10 firstbit (141304/152173/152173 across three byte-identical runs) and persists with -presolve off, so the noise comes from Gurobi (multithreaded, per-peel-layer TimeLimit at internal/mip/mip.go:362), not from presolve. That noise exceeds the effect being measured.

arms.on2: hops.Cache enabled, repeated -- control that separates 'cache is impure' from 'cand is nondeterministic'
arms.off: hops.Cache.SetEnabled(false) -- recomputes every query, retains nothing

bench_configs.note: -repeat R replays the family list R times to simulate consecutive rounds reusing the cache; -reps N runs each arm N times so the wall clock is a best-of-N, because single runs on this box swing 2-3x.

reference: For recall only: an in-process brute-force enumeration of every node (excluding the demand's own source/target) as a single waypoint, routed for real and kept when it strictly relieves a target, top-12 by relief. This is the legacy generator's own node ranking, so it isolates what the targeted search kept of it. It is a LOWER BOUND on the MIP's option set because cand's 2-waypoint output (79% of its candidates) has no counterpart in it.

headline_results.bug_fixed: internal/cand/strategies.go crossedHotArcs ranged a map (want) instead of the arcs slice. bottleneck bans in the returned order and stops at MaxBans (default 3), so when a demand crossed more than 3 hot arcs WHICH arcs were banned was random -- and with them the detour node set, the paired candidates and the MIP columns. Fixed to range arcs; regression test TestBuildIsRepeatableUnderMapOrderRandomisation verified to FAIL before the fix and pass after (ladderInstance, 6 tight arcs, MaxBans=2, 64 Build calls).
headline_results.determinism: PASS 20/20 (two identical cache-on runs give bit-identical candidate lists)
headline_results.cache_neutrality: PASS 20/20 (cache-on vs cache-off give bit-identical candidate lists). Before the fix, setA-02/04/10 FAILED -- that was cand's nondeterminism, not the cache.
headline_results.cache_bfs: on 1168 vs off 40560 over the same 40680 queries = 34.7x fewer BFS computations (39392 saved), 97.1% of queries served from the map
headline_results.cache_wall: 6052 ms vs 6484 ms best-of-3 = 7.1% faster. The BFS was never the bottleneck: ~25 UnitRoute calls per family dominate.
headline_results.relief_capture_below_1: setA-04 0.9381, setA-10 0.9797, setA-13 0.9371, setA-16 0.9205 -- these instances LOSE the single best singleton the brute-force ranking finds. setA-10/13/16 are the instances where the full-solve A/B also underperformed, making this the most likely mechanism behind the setA-10 regression (97826 -> ~150k).
headline_results.degenerate_families: 206/725 families (28.4%) return no candidate. Concentrated: setA-15 (30/38 empty, 1.1 w1/family), setA-17 (30/35, 2.1), setA-20 (32/60, 1.1). setA-18 is 60/60 empty and correct: its hottest arc 163 (sat 0.999998765) is the class-1 bridge presolve proved in 2026-09-10_02, so no single waypoint can relieve it and the first bit is optimal at the start.
headline_results.timing_caveat: A single-run sweep (solution/runs_candbench2, kept as a counter-example) reported the cache as 2x SLOWER (setA-20 2625 vs 1038 ms); five paired repeats of the identical config gave 479-571 ms vs 536-630 ms with on<off in 5/5. Wall-clock conclusions below 30% require best-of-N pairing; only the BFS counters are noise-free.

tunables_for_next_step.recall_lower_bound: recall@12 compares against single-waypoint brute force only; the 2-waypoint side is not covered by it and is 79% of cand's output.
tunables_for_next_step.cheap_fix_for_capture: the single-waypoint brute force is O(n) real routings per family (~1 s for 60 families at n=400), so a global relief top-K singleton strategy can be added at low cost to restore capture to 1.0 on the four instances.
tunables_for_next_step.ball_pressure: MaxExtraHop=4 is too tight for setA-15/17/20 (w1/family collapses to 1-2, most families empty). A size- or fill-adaptive radius would help but conflicts with design doc 12 Q7, which forbids a size-adaptive default mode.
